steps.body: Bigger grids just mean more squares to count — the counting idea never changes, even when the grid grows.

widget.prompt: A rectangle is partitioned into 5 rows and 5 columns of unit squares. How many unit squares in all?

commonCounts.feedback: That's 5 + 5. Count every square in the grid: 25.
That's just one row. Count all 5 rows: 25 in all.

widget.successFeedback: 5 rows of 5 squares each makes 25 squares in all.

steps.body: A short, wide grid can have the same total as a tall, narrow one — 2 rows of 7 and 7 rows of 2 both give 14 squares.

commonCounts.feedback: That's 2 + 7. Count every square in the grid: 14.
That's just one column. Count all 7 columns in both rows: 14 in all.

steps.body: This means the shape of the grid can change while the total stays the same — as long as rows and columns trade places.
Predict, then check: does flipping the grid change the total?

predict.prompt: This grid will have 9 rows of 4 squares each. If you flipped it to 4 rows of 9 squares instead, would the total be more, fewer, or the same?
predict.reveal: 9 rows of 4 is 36, and 4 rows of 9 is also 36 — flipping the grid trades rows for columns, but every square is still counted once, so the total never changes.

widget.prompt: The grid below has 9 rows and 4 columns of unit squares. Count them to check your prediction.

commonCounts.feedback: That's 9 + 4. Count every square in the grid: 36.
That's just one column. Count all 9 rows: 36 in all.

widget.successFeedback: 9 rows of 4 squares each makes 36 squares in all — the same total as 4 rows of 9, just flipped.
widget.lowFeedback: 9 rows of 4 squares each makes 36 squares in all.
widget.highFeedback: 9 rows of 4 squares each makes 36 squares in all.

steps.body: Add a row, not a column.
explanationVariants: Adding a row adds one full new row of 7: 21+7=28.
4 rows of 7 columns is 28 — a new row changes the row count, not the column count.

widget.prompt: A grid starts with 3 rows of 7 unit squares each. One more row of 7 is added, making 4 rows in all. How many unit squares are in the grid now?

commonCounts.feedback: That's the total BEFORE the new row was added. Now there are 4 rows of 7: count all of them for 28.
That's just the NEW row. Add it to the 3 rows that were already there: 4 rows of 7 is 28.

widget.successFeedback: 4 rows of 7 unit squares each makes 28 squares in all — one whole new row of 7 was added to the original 21.
widget.lowFeedback: 4 rows of 7 unit squares each makes 28 squares in all.
widget.highFeedback: 4 rows of 7 unit squares each makes 28 squares in all.

steps.body: Add a column, not a row.
explanationVariants: Adding a column adds one square to each of the 8 rows: 24+8=32.
8 rows of 4 columns is 32 — a new column changes the column count, not the row count.

widget.prompt: A grid has 8 rows of 3 unit squares each. If one more COLUMN (not a row) is added, how many unit squares will the grid have in all?

commonCounts.feedback: That's the total BEFORE the new column was added. Adding a column adds one more square to EACH of the 8 rows: 24+8=32.
That adds 3 (a row's worth), but a COLUMN was added, not a row. A new column adds one square to each of the 8 rows: 24+8=32.

widget.successFeedback: 8 rows of 3 becomes 8 rows of 4 once a column is added: 8×4=32 unit squares in all.
widget.lowFeedback: 8 rows of 4 unit squares each makes 32 squares in all.
widget.highFeedback: 8 rows of 4 unit squares each makes 32 squares in all.

steps.body: Watch for a different kind of mix-up this time.
explanationVariants: 7 rows of 7 squares each is 49 squares in all — that counts every square inside, not the distance around the edge.
The edge around the grid is the PERIMETER; the squares filling it are the AREA. Count the squares: 49.

widget.prompt: This grid has 7 rows and 7 columns of unit squares. Count only the squares — not the edge around the grid.

commonCounts.feedback: That's 2 × (7 + 7) — the PERIMETER (the distance around the edge), not the area. Count every square filling the inside instead: 49.
That's just one row. Count all 7 rows: 49 in all.

widget.successFeedback: 7 rows of 7 squares each makes 49 squares in all.
widget.lowFeedback: 7 rows of 7 squares each makes 49 squares in all.
widget.highFeedback: 7 rows of 7 squares each makes 49 squares in all.

hints: Count every square INSIDE the grid — not the distance around the outside edge.

steps.body: Bigger grids still count the same way — every square, in every row.
takeaways: Bigger grids mean more squares, but the same counting idea.
Rows and columns can trade places and give the same total.
Count every square in the grid, however big it is.
